claims.claim: Augustine of Hippo was bishop of Hippo from 396 to 430.
Augustine was born on November 13, 354, in Tagaste, Numidia, and died on August 28, 430, in Hippo Regius.
Augustine wrote On Care to Be Had for the Dead in response to a letter from Paulinus asking whether it profits any person after death that his body shall be buried at the memorial of any Saint.
The work was addressed to Paulinus, whom Augustine calls his 'venerable fellow-bishop.'

The occasion for the work arose when the widow Flora begged Paulinus to have her deceased son Cynegius buried at the basilica of most blessed Felix the Confessor, which was done, and Paulinus then wrote to Augustine with the same question.

Paulinus himself believed that the care for deceased friends was not empty motions of religious and faithful minds, and that the whole Church's supplication for the departed could not be void of effect.
The work survives as part of Augustine's corpus and is included in the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers series.
Augustine was one of the Latin Fathers of the Church and is formally recognized as a doctor of the church in Roman Catholicism.
Augustine's adaptation of classical thought to Christian teaching created a theological system of great power and lasting influence.
Augustine was a massively prolific writer whose life and writings go hand-in-hand, and he is highly unusual among ancient thinkers in terms of how much has been preserved both from and about him.
